chunks: 38. And with the former chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hadid, who said: Abu Ishaq al-Khorasani, a companion of ours, informed me saying: The Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, used to say:

Do not harbor doubt, lest you become skeptics; and do not be skeptics, lest you fall into disbelief. Do not be lenient with yourselves, lest you become sycophants; and do not compromise in matters of truth, lest you suffer loss.

Verily, firmness lies in gaining deep understanding of religion, and part of true religious understanding is not to be deceived. Indeed, the most sincere of you toward himself is the most obedient of you to his Lord, and the most deceitful of you toward himself is the most disobedient of you to his Lord.

Whoever obeys Allah is secure and guided, and whoever disobeys Him is disappointed and filled with regret. Ask Allah for certitude, and turn to Him for well-being, for the best thing that resides in the heart is certitude.
O people! Beware of lying, for every one who hopes is a seeker, and every one who fears is a fleeing one.

key_terms.الحزم: Firmness, prudence, and sound judgment in religious matters
key_terms.العافية: Well-being, safety, and divine protection from spiritual and physical harm
key_terms.الفقه: Deep understanding of religion, not merely jurisprudence but comprehensive religious insight
key_terms.المداهنة: Sycophancy, flattering or compromising truth for worldly gain
key_terms.اليقين: Certitude, firm conviction in faith beyond mere belief

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the relationship between doubt, religious understanding, and sincerity?
ai.summary: In this sermon transmitted through Ali ibn Mahzyar, Ali ibn Hadid, and Abu Ishaq al-Khorasani, Imam Ali (AS) delivers a powerful exhortation to the believers about the dangers of spiritual complacency. He establishes a chain of spiritual deterioration: doubt leads to skepticism, skepticism leads to disbelief, self-indulgence leads to sycophancy, and compromising truth leads to loss. He emphasizes that true firmness comes from deep religious learning, and that sincerity toward oneself is measured by obedience to God.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 38. And with the former chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar (from ‘Ali ibn Hadeed), who reported from Abu Ishaq al-Khorasani, a friend of ours, that: Amirul Mu’mineen, ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, used to say:

"Do not be shaken in your faith, for that will make you a doubter; and do not be doubters, for that will lead to disbelief. And do not make yourself cheap falling victim to flattery and adulation; and do not be sycophant in matters of truth, for that will cause you a great loss.

Firmness lies in becoming more learned in Religion and the sign of true religious learning is not to be conceited nor deceitful. The most honest and sincere to oneself among you is the one who is most obedient to his Sustainer; and the most deceitful to oneself among you is the one who is most insubordinate to his Sustainer.

He who obeys Him, is secure and guided; and he who disobeys Him, is disappointed and remorseful. Seek certitude from Allah and set your hearts inclined to Him, when you are free from all harm; for the best experience of heart is that of certitude.
O people! refrain from lying. And anyone who expects, proceeds to demand and anyone who fears, flees."
